# Was the Delta weight-and-balance outage a cyberattack?

**Not established.** Not established. Delta says only that it was a technical or automation issue and gives no cause. The FAA says the delays are not related to FAA air traffic systems. Nobody has claimed or confirmed an attack.

Incident: Delta weight-and-balance outage, Nov 22, 2026. Also reported as Delta outage, Delta Atlanta ground stop and Delta ALIS outage. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 4:46 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Delta Air Lines, the FAA, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 4:46 PM ET: **ABC's updated count: more than 1,600 Delta flights delayed, per Delta.** ABC updated its story (4:43 PM ET): citing Delta, more than 1,600 Delta flights were delayed Sunday and about 49% of Delta flights ran more than 15 minutes late. c006 now uses the updated figures; the earlier 1,300 count is superseded. No label changes.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. More than 1,600 Delta flights were delayed on Nov 22, per ABC citing Delta, during the start of Thanksgiving travel. Delta says about 5,000 flights were scheduled that day.
- Who is affected: Delta and Delta Connection passengers on Sunday, Nov 22, mainly at Atlanta and on flights into it. Delta says it is rebooking customers and offering meals, hotels and refunds.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1,600+ | Delta flights delayed | ABC, citing Delta |
| 11:26 AM | Ground delay lifted | NBC News, Eastern time |
| ~70% | Delays tied to automation | Delta, of ~5,000 flights |

### Known so far

- Delta's weight-and-balance automation system went down on Sunday, Nov 22; crews used manual workarounds.
- The FAA stopped Atlanta-bound Delta flights at Delta's request, then eased it to a Delta-only delay just after 8:40 AM ET.

### Not known yet

- What caused the outage. Delta gives no cause.
- Whether a cyberattack was involved. No official statement addresses it either way.
- Whether it relates to the FAA's Nov 13 ground stop or United's Nov 16 outage.
